content:
Rina Kobayashi: heads up, benchmark-lab PR is up for the fragmentation workload generator: https://github.com/benchmark-lab/pull/881

Rina Kobayashi: before we bake this into perf canary, can someone sanity check whether the churn pattern actually looks like prod? esp cancellations + mixed seq lens.

Marcus Reed: thx. i skimmed the PR but haven’t run it yet. what’s the target behavior? “allocator fragmentation under sustained decode w/ request churn” right?

Omar El-Sayed: yep. we want to recreate the bad pattern we see in hosted: long-lived sessions + a lot of short ones coming/going, mixed prompt lens, plus occasional cancels (client disconnect / timeout).

Samir Qureshi: +1. fragmentation in our KV arena isn’t just random. it’s basically: some sequences hold on to big contiguous blocks for a long time, then churn fills holes with smaller allocations, and then those holes never line up again.

Rina Kobayashi: current generator uses: 
- prompt_len sampled from {128..4096} log-uniform
- decode_len sampled from {64..2048} log-uniform
- 15% “long-lived” sessions (fixed for N minutes)
- rest are single-shot requests
- optional cancels (currently 2%)

Rina Kobayashi: but i’m not sure it matches our production “burstiness” or the cancel distribution.

Allison Grant: from an observability POV, what matters is: does it drive the fragmentation_ratio + bytes_moved + eviction_count dynamics similarly to prod. we should compare the time-series shape, not just peak.

Julian Moore: prod traces show cancels are spiky, not constant. usually a retry storm or a frontend timeout sweep.

Sahana Iyer: also in CI/perf we’re sensitive to non-determinism. if we add burstiness, can we seed it so runs are repeatable?

Rina Kobayashi: yep generator is seeded; bursts are a schedule.

Marcus Reed: question: in prod, we see streaming responses, and a bunch of clients disconnect mid-stream. does the generator simulate “disconnect during decode” or just “cancel before prefill finishes”? those behave differently in runtime.

Omar El-Sayed: the nasty edge case is cancel during relocation / compaction step, but for fragmentation itself it’s mostly “sequence dies while holding pages” + churn creates holes.

Samir Qureshi: still, we should include cancel mid-decode. that’s what leaks/strands pages if we mess up bookkeeping. i know there’s a follow-up test ticket, but workload generator should poke it.

Rina Kobayashi: currently cancels are implemented as: pick active request, send cancel after X decode steps (uniform between 5..50 steps). so it’s mid-decode.

Lena Fischer: do we simulate backpressure / admission? prod has shed under burst sometimes, which changes churn pattern (lots of short-lived rejected requests). that can mask fragmentation unless you pin concurrency.

Marcus Reed: yeah. if the generator drives the system into overload, it might not reflect the “sustained decode at ~80-90% util” we care about.

Rina Kobayashi: generator can run at fixed concurrency (N in-flight) or fixed RPS. default in PR is fixed concurrency.

Yuki Sato: what’s the GPU copy/move budget assumption? if this is meant to validate compaction, we should avoid pathological micro-batching patterns that don’t happen in prod.

Omar El-Sayed: our prod-ish pattern: 
- lots of 128-512 prompt
- fewer 2k-4k prompt
- decode lens tends to be bimodal: very short (<128) and medium (~512-1024). super long decode exists but not dominating.
- “long-lived” sessions are mostly chatty but with think time.

Omar El-Sayed: does generator include think time between turns, or are long-lived sessions just continuously decoding back-to-back?

Rina Kobayashi: long-lived sessions in current generator do back-to-back turns with a small fixed sleep (50ms) but not a realistic distribution.

Marcus Reed: 50ms is basically “no think time” for humans. prod chat think time is seconds, but the *KV allocation* stays alive while idle, which is kind of the point.

Samir Qureshi: exactly. fragmentation happens because those big allocations stay pinned while others churn. we want idle gaps, not constant decode.

Julian Moore: +1. real: session lives for 10-30 min but only generates intermittently. that keeps blocks reserved, and the allocator has to pack around them.

Rina Kobayashi: ok, so we should change long-lived behavior to: keep session allocated, but only issue a turn every e.g. 2-10s (random), with occasional bursts (multi-turn in short window).

Sahana Iyer: careful: if think time is long, benchmark duration needs to be longer to see the fragmentation accumulate. can we speed up time while still preserving allocation lifetimes?

Marcus Reed: could do “logical think time” without wall clock: i.e. sleep scaled, but keep session alive for the same number of scheduler ticks.

Allison Grant: if you do that, document it. otherwise people will interpret the benchmark as “this is real-time.”

Rina Kobayashi: noted.

Lena Fischer: do we have prod churn stats? like distribution of session lifetime, inter-arrival, cancel probability, etc.

Julian Moore: rough numbers from traces last week (hosted, us-east-1):
- ~8-12% connections drop mid-stream on bursty workloads
- 90p session lifetime ~18 min, but median ~2-3 min
- inter-turn think time (chat) median ~4-6s, long tail
- cancel storms happen when frontend deploy + timeout mismatch (lots of 30s timeouts)

Julian Moore: i can paste more once i scrub the customer ids.

Omar El-Sayed: this is useful. our generator currently has cancel_prob fixed; we should add “cancel storm windows” (e.g. for 60s every 10 min, cancel_prob jumps from 2% -> 15%).

Samir Qureshi: +1, and it should correlate with burst in new sessions. storms are usually “lots of new requests + lots of cancels” (retries).

Rina Kobayashi: i can add a burst schedule:
- every T seconds, ramp short-lived arrivals by factor B for D seconds
- during that window, raise cancel prob and lower client timeout

Rina Kobayashi: something like:
```yaml
bursts:
  - every_s: 600
    duration_s: 90
    arrival_multiplier: 3.0
    cancel_prob: 0.12
    timeout_ms: 30000
```

Sahana Iyer: please keep defaults stable + add a “prod_churn” preset. CI can run a smaller deterministic preset and nightly can run prod-ish.

Allison Grant: also: can we output a small summary block at end of run with realized distributions? (actual prompt lens, cancel rate, session lifetime). helps debug when someone changes config.

Rina Kobayashi: yes, i can print percentiles + hist bins.

Marcus Reed: other concern: prompt_len distribution in PR is log-uniform. prod is closer to log-normal / mixture, and there are hard peaks (common prompt templates). do we need that fidelity?

Omar El-Sayed: i don’t think we need exact, but we do need the “many small, some large” skew and mixed allocations. mixture distribution is probably closer.

Samir Qureshi: +1. fragmentation sensitivity depends on the gap between “small allocations used to fill holes” and “big long-lived allocations.” mixture will behave more like prod.

Rina Kobayashi: i’ll change to a mixture:
- 70% prompts: 128-512 (weighted)
- 25% prompts: 512-2048
- 5% prompts: 2048-4096
and decode mixture too.

Yuki Sato: pls make sure we don’t accidentally create a ton of tiny decodes that never hit steady-state decode kernels. we want sustained decode pressure, otherwise compaction budget behavior won’t show.

Marcus Reed: right. maybe enforce minimum decode steps for a subset so there’s always a background of “ongoing decode.”

Rina Kobayashi: i can add a “sticky decode cohort” (e.g. 10% of requests forced to decode >= 512 tokens).

Lena Fischer: can we also include tier mix? hosted has free/paid tiers with different priority; eviction policy is tier-aware.

Omar El-Sayed: workload generator can tag requests with priority. but benchmark-lab doesn’t know about our tier routing unless we plumb headers.

Rina Kobayashi: PR currently supports adding arbitrary headers per request group. we can add groups:
- tier=pro (60%)
- tier=enterprise (30%)
- tier=free (10%)

Allison Grant: and then metrics should break down eviction_count by tier label. (otherwise it’s hard to validate correctness of tier-aware eviction).

Samir Qureshi: +1.

Sahana Iyer: action item: Rina update PR with (1) think time model, (2) bursty cancel windows, (3) mixture dists, (4) end-of-run realized stats, (5) tier headers. then Marcus + Omar can re-run against staging runtime builds.

Rina Kobayashi: sounds good. i’ll push updates today and ping.

Marcus Reed: once it’s updated, i’ll run side-by-side with prod trace replay (limited) to compare fragmentation_ratio shape and p99 spikes.

Julian Moore: i’ll pull the scrubbed churn stats and drop them here so we can tune defaults.

Allison Grant: and please align metric names in the generator output with the metric standard doc (fragmentation_ratio, kv_bytes_moved_total, kv_compaction_time_ms, kv_evictions_total). we’ve been bitten by “almost same name” before.

Rina Kobayashi: ack. will do.

Rina Kobayashi: (also adding a README snippet explaining “logical think time” if we go that route)

Omar El-Sayed: :thumbsup: thanks. once we’re happy, we can wire it into perf-canary scenario ticket.

BenchBot: CI run started for benchmark-lab#881 (seed=1337, profile=fragmentation_default)

Samir Qureshi: lol BenchBot already on it

Rina Kobayashi: :sweat_smile: i’ll update configs before we care about those results
